We need a retrosynthesis route with at most 1 step (i.e., direct synthesis from commercially available precursors). The target is COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. This looks like a methyl ester of a bicyclic ketone (maybe methyl 1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalene-1-carboxylate? Actually structure: a bicyclic [2.2.1] maybe? Let's decode: COC(=O) attached to a chiral carbon bridging two rings? The SMILES: COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. That's methyl ester of a bicyclic ketone (maybe methyl 1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalene-1-carboxylate). The core is a bicyclic fused ring with a ketone at C2? Might be methyl 1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalene-1-carboxylate (also known as methyl 1-naphthoate? Not exactly). Anyway, we need a single-step retrosynthesis: maybe from methyl 2-oxocyclohex-1-ene-1-carboxylate? But we need commercially available chemicals.

Potential route: esterification of the corresponding carboxylic acid with methanol. So precursor could be the carboxylic acid: O=C([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)O (i.e., the same skeleton but acid instead of methyl ester). Is that commercially available? Likely not.

Alternative: use a known building block like methyl 2-oxocyclohex-1-ene-1-carboxylate? Not same.

Maybe the target is methyl 1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalene-1-carboxylate (also called methyl tetralin-1-carboxylate). Tetralin-1-carboxylic acid is commercially available? Possibly. Tetralin (1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalene) is common. Tetralin-1-carboxylic acid maybe available. Methyl ester can be made by Fischer esterification (acid + methanol). That's a single-step reaction (acid + MeOH, acid catalyst). But the route must be retrosynthetic: we need precursors that are commercially available chemicals. So we can propose the reaction: esterification of tetralin-1-carboxylic acid (SMILES: O=C(O)C1CC=CC2=CC=CC=C12? Wait need correct SMILES). Let's generate: Tetralin-1-carboxylic acid: O=C(O)C1CC=CC2=CC=CC=C12? Actually tetralin is C1CCCc2ccccc2C1. Carboxylic acid at position 1 (bridgehead). SMILES: O=C(O)C1CCc2ccccc2C1. But our target has a ketone at the other bridgehead (C(C2)=O). So there is a carbonyl inside the ring as well. So it's not just tetralin-1-carboxylate; there is also a ketone at the other bridgehead (C(C2)=O). So the skeleton is a bicyclic with two carbonyls: one ketone inside ring, one ester outside.

Thus maybe the precursor is the corresponding acid (same skeleton) which can be esterified. Is that acid commercially available? Possibly not.

Alternative: start from methyl 2-oxotetralin-1-carboxylate? That is exactly our target? Wait target has both a ketone and an ester. So the acid version would have a carboxylic acid and a ketone. That might be commercially available as "tetralone-1-carboxylic acid"? Not sure.

Maybe we can propose a single-step from two commercially available reagents via a condensation (e.g., acylation of a ketone with methoxy carbonyl chloride). For example, start from the ketone (tetralone) and react with methyl chloroformate (or methyl carbonochloridate) to form the ester at the alpha carbon? But the ester is attached to the same carbon as the ketone? Actually the carbon bearing the ester is a bridgehead carbon attached to the ketone carbonyl on adjacent carbon. The ester carbonyl is attached to that carbon (C=O OCH3). So it's a carboxylate attached to the same carbon as the ketone? Wait SMILES: COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. The central carbon is attached to OCH3 and carbonyl O (ester) and also attached to the bicyclic skeleton. So it's a carbonyl carbon of the ester attached to the chiral carbon. So the carbon is the carbonyl carbon of the ester, not the same as the ketone carbon. The ketone is on the other bridgehead: C(C2)=O. So we have a bicyclic system with a ketone at one bridgehead and an ester carbonyl attached to the other bridgehead (as a carbonyl carbon). So the precursor could be the acid (same skeleton) which can be esterified. So we need the acid: O=C(O)[C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O. That is "tetralin-1-carboxylic acid with a ketone at position 2"? Might be "2-oxotetralin-1-carboxylic acid". Could be commercially available? Possibly.

Let's check if that acid is buyable.
